ra: The one God of the Samaritans is the central object of the tradition's worship; placed in the cohort hub.
Moses, the supreme Samaritan prophet, is a core member of the cohort.
The Taheb is the Samaritan eschatological figure within the cohort.
Marqah is the foundational Samaritan theologian in the cohort.
Baba Rabba, the reformer, belongs to the Samaritan cohort.
The high-priestly office is a core institution of the cohort.
Phinehas, ancestor of the priestly line, belongs to the cohort.
Mount Gerizim, the sacred realm, anchors the cohort.
The divine Glory is a theological concept within the cohort.
The Angel/Malak belongs to the Samaritan cohort.
The Samaritan Torah is the canon of the cohort.
The Gerizim Passover sacrifice is a core ritual of the cohort.
Joseph, ancestor of the Samaritans, belongs to the cohort.
Joshua, who founded Gerizim worship, belongs to the cohort.
The Rahuta/Fanuta periodization is a cosmological concept of the cohort.
In Samaritan theology Moses is the sole revealer of the complete Torah.
Marqah's Memar Marqah is the foundational theological exposition transmitting Samaritan Torah doctrine.
Marqah's Memar Marqah develops the doctrine of the divine Glory/Light upon Moses.
The Glory is God's own manifest presence/Light proceeding from the one God.
The created Angel/Malak mediates God's word and presence in Samaritan theology.
The Glory shone upon and was made manifest through Moses at Sinai per Memar Marqah.
The Samaritan high priest presides over the annual Passover sacrifice on Gerizim.
The Samaritan Passover sacrifice is performed on Mount Gerizim, the chosen place.
The Samaritan high-priestly line is traced from Phinehas (the Pinhasite priesthood).
In Samaritan tradition Joshua established the sanctuary on Gerizim, inaugurating the Rahuta.
Joshua's establishment of Gerizim worship inaugurates the era of divine Favor (Rahuta).
Baba Rabba operated in close concert with the priesthood in reorganizing the community.
The Taheb is expected to restore true worship and recover the hidden vessels on Mount Gerizim.
The Taheb is understood as the prophet like Moses (Deut 18:18) who restores Mosaic worship.
The Samaritan supreme prophet Moses is a tradition-specific reception of the Israelite Moses; same scriptural figure, distinct theological elevation. Homonym across traditions.
Samaritan Joshua (builder of the Gerizim altar) receives the Israelite Joshua. Homonym.
Samaritans claim descent through Joseph (Ephraim/Manasseh); their Joseph is a reception of the Pentateuchal Joseph. Homonym.
Phinehas son of Eleazar son of Aaron; the Samaritan priestly line descends from Aaron via Phinehas. Linked to the existing Israelite Aaron.
The one God of the Samaritans is the same God of Israel (Yahweh/the tetragrammaton); a shared Israelite deity worshipped under a distinct Gerizim cult.
The Taheb expectation as a returning prophet-like-Moses functionally aligns with the prophet-of-restoration role; modern cross-tradition functional alignment, not identity.

The Samaritan divine Glory/Kavod is a functional cognate of the Jewish Shekhinah/Kavod as God's manifest presence; parallel mediating concepts in sister Israelite traditions (modern comparative alignment, not identity).
